elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The inserted warranty covers only conformance of the Services "in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement"; no professional/workmanlike or industry-standard performance standard appears anywhere in Section 9 or the insertion.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: "the Site and any software provided by HDI hereunder will conform in all material respects to their documentation".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The inserted software warranty runs "for ninety (90) days following the Effective Date", not 12 months.
The inserted Services warranty runs "for thirty (30) days following performance", short of 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "The Company's remedy for breach of this warranty is repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or Services..."
"...or a refund of the fees paid for them."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Neither the retained Section 9(a) corporate-authority representations nor the insertion contains any compliance-with-laws warranty; the drafter expressly declined this element.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code / virus warranty appears in the rendered language; the drafter expressly declined this element.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "for ninety (90) days following the Effective Date, the Site and any software provided by HDI hereunder will conform in all material respects to their documentation" — express software-to-documentation warranty of exactly 90 days (deterministic period check ok).

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: "for thirty (30) days following performance, the Services will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement" — 30-day services warranty running from performance.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "The Company's remedy for breach of this warranty is repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or Services"; remedy is not restricted to Vendor's election, which is favourable to us.
"or a refund of the fees paid for them" — refund of fees paid for the non-conforming software or Services.

reasons: Finding status "missing" is correct on the record: Section 9(a) is limited to mutual corporate-existence/authority representations and 9(b) is a Globix acknowledgement, so no express performance, conformance or remedy warranty existed; no "AS IS" disclaimer competes with the insertion.

Fallback level is position-complete: the single inserted sentence pair supplies (i) a 90-day software-to-documentation warranty, (ii) a 30-day Services warranty, and (iii) repair or replacement and refund remedies. All four fallback elements are met in operative language, not merely promised in the comment.

Preferred level is not met and is not claimed: the 12-month software period, 90-day services period, professional-and-workmanlike standard, compliance-with-laws warranty and no-malicious-code warranty are all absent.

Minimality holds: the edit is a pure insertion into an existing warranty section, deletes nothing, retains the favourable Globix carve-out in 9(b), and adds no survival tail, notice procedure, at-own-expense language or damages category beyond the four selected elements. Specifying a conformance standard for the Services is necessary content for the 30-day element, not an extra.

Intent is preserved: the mutual representations, the Globix mechanic and Article 1 delivery/operation obligations survive without contradiction, and no cross-reference is left dangling by the insertion.

Repair recommended (not element-fatal): anchor the software warranty to delivery/launch acceptance of the Site rather than "following the Effective Date". In a development-and-hosting agreement the Site is built after execution, so a 90-day window measured from the Effective Date could expire before the software is delivered; change to "ninety (90) days following delivery of the Site (and of each software component provided by HDI)" to make the coverage real.

Second check for the drafter: confirm that "Services" is a defined term elsewhere in the Agreement. If it is not, the capitalized reference in the insertion creates an undefined term — substitute "the services performed by HDI under Article 1" to avoid an interpretive gap.

Optional low-cost asks that remain available on the next pass and would not disturb the fallback: adding "professional and workmanlike manner" for the Services and a no-malicious-code warranty for hosted Site software.
